entries.claim: Any parseable record that satisfies `isReadsRotationMarker` is treated as authoritative rotation metadata and removed from the read records.
entries.failure_scenario: A tool-call record is untrusted JSON and can forge the rotation shape (for example, `{ "event": "reads_rotation", "file": "reads.1.jsonl", "ts": "...", "agent": "worker", ... }`). This code drops that real call from all summaries/join results and emits `reads.rotated`, falsely claiming the record was cut. Conversely, a forged later marker can overwrite the metadata from a genuine marker because `rotated` is assigned for every matching line.

counter_evidence.note: recordFromHook builds every reads record from a fixed key set - ts, tool, agent, agent_id, tool_use_id, target, offset, limit, mode, files, bytes - copies no attacker-controlled key through, and always sets tool from RECORDED_TOOLS. isReadsRotationMarker at line 133 requires !("tool" in record), so no record the hook can produce satisfies the predicate and no tool call can forge a marker. The finding's own example also carries event: "reads_rotation", which is not the READS_ROTATION constant ("record_rotated") the predicate compares against. The overwrite half fails on the same construction: rotateReads writes exactly one marker into a file that is fresh by rename, so a live record holds at most one marker line.

entries.claim: Malformed JSON is skipped indiscriminately, including a truncated rotation marker that is the only evidence that the live reads record was cut.
entries.failure_scenario: If rotation has moved the old record aside and the process is killed while writing the first marker line of the new `reads.jsonl`, the truncated marker fails `JSON.parse` and is silently skipped. `readReadsRecords` then returns no `rotated` field at line 378, so both `reads` and `trace suggest` report the run record as not cut even though the rotated sibling was already created.

counter_evidence.note: The marker is never written into the live path incrementally. rotateReads writes the whole marker line to a private temp with writeFileSync(temp, ..., {flag: "wx"}) and then renameSync(temp, file), so the live reads.jsonl is swapped atomically and a process killed mid-write leaves the temp behind, cleaned by the finally arm, never a truncated marker at the live path. The scenario requires a partial first line to become visible at the live path, which this construction does not permit.
